newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-Australian bonds batten down for U.S. jobs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds batten down for U.S. jobs.

text.p: *Australian bonds kept to a fairly narrow range after their initial run-up as the market battened down for Friday's key U.S. labour force report.
*Market seen around fair value based on current data.
Australian bond prices kept to a fairly narrow range after their initial run up as the market battened down for Friday's key U.S. labour force report.

Shortcovering after stage two of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony gave no new major concerns over current policy thinking and formed the base for the day's trading, but there was little interest in taking the rally too far, traders said.
They added that the local market is now around fair value after the volatile movements seen in the last couple of weeks based on the current data flow.
The next local major hurdle will be the February labour force report in a week's time, but the U.S. jobs data will set the early tone for the week, traders said.

They also felt that domestic bonds, while firmer, are still taking a defensive role after the complete turn-around in sentiment from anticipating another easing in monetary policy to now predicting a tightening by year-end.
December bill futures at 93.25 are still pricing in a 75 basis point tightening in current 6.0 percent official interest rates, by maturity.

The local market's paring of its early advance saw spread differentials to the dollar bloc show a marginal widening bias. The market had made a strong outperformance on Wednesday as the recent sharp blow-out was partially corrected.
